items.rationale: The checker faithfully expresses the selected conditional interpretation: after a first pre-publication failure, a successful second Close requires Open of the same snapshot to succeed. The harness calls actual methods sequentially and retains one operation ID and the actual sink ID throughout. Check e42984b16b94474ea0f8ba978ff4872f records a complete buffered Write, a first Close flush failure on the closed file, an absent publication directory, a nil second Close result, and Open failing because the published metadata path does not exist. Thus the antecedent occurred and the conditional assertion is false in this adapted execution. The snapshot_open event spans two Go test output records; those Output strings must be concatenated before parsing the event. Source behavior explains the observations: Close sets closed before finalize, exits on its failure before rename, and subsequently returns nil without publication work. Open independently reads the final directory. However, the successful-end comment describes Close's purpose without explicitly guaranteeing that repeated calls report the original finalization outcome; ID's documentation promises usability only after finalization. The idempotence comment supports an alternative interpretation in which repeated Close merely acknowledges closure. The checker therefore measures the proposed result-to-availability discrepancy but cannot settle whether that discrepancy violates the applicable contract. Its legality conditions establish experimental setup, not authorization of private descriptor closure as a production fault. Even satisfaction of this local obligation would not establish durable recovery, valid application contents, or safe reclamation; those responsibilities are outside this check.
counterevidence: FileSnapshotSink.Close explicitly treats an already-closed sink as an idempotent no-op returning nil. This is contrary evidence to the proposed repeated-call interpretation, although implementation behavior alone does not establish the contract.

The SnapshotSink interface says that errors lead to Cancel and does not explicitly promise persistent Close errors or publication on a repeated Close. The successful-end comment can describe caller intent rather than an unconditional postcondition of every nil return.
The harness closes a private stateFile descriptor. No supplied fault contract establishes that this internal intervention represents a legal production execution.

takeSnapshot returns before metadata advancement and compaction when Persist or its own Close reports an error. The experiment does not exercise a caller that legally proceeds after observing the initial failure.
limitations: The Go test PASS indicates successful completion of observation and prerequisite checks; the harness contains no assertion enforcing the publication property. No separate monitor-evaluation receipt is supplied.
The actual trace supports missing publication, rather than an unrelated Open failure, through matching snapshot identity, the metadata ENOENT result, and independent directory observations.

Resolving applicability requires attributable documentation or contract evidence defining repeated Close after failure, and evidence supporting an applicable storage-fault mechanism. No exact location for such additional material is supplied; a targeted repository discovery follow-up is needed before a bounded source-range request can be specified.
Configuration validation is observed as successful, but configuration.go:1:350 is not attached for independent inspection of its implementation.
The result covers one sequential adapted execution. It establishes neither production reachability nor metadata advancement, log deletion, crash durability, or loss of recoverable history.
Preserve the measured return-to-availability discrepancy as an adapted execution result; do not promote it to a confirmed contract violation while the substantive applicability disputes remain open.
